notes: Known-ledger rows for these files (e.g. code-style NIT-91..103/114/118-122 r1, NIT-27/28/30-33/36 r2, MIN-86/87/104) suppressed; variants skipped: sync_skills.sh repeated off/on merge jq (variant of NIT-100), nightly run.sh 4x routine_allowed_tools/flags/claude-p stage block (overlaps MIN-86). Non-Go files answered against the Go groups with empty hits (groups not applicable). Cross-chunk/cross-direction suspicion for the station: cmd/hooks/skill-invoke-gate.sh:52 deny text tells the lane to invoke the skill 'bare, no args', contradicting railroad-review SKILL-RAILROADREVIEW-CTX-002a (lanes MUST pass args="lane:<direction>"); an agent obeying the message would get the full context set instead of its direction slice. Doc drift: README.md:76 install.ps1 prereq row omits shellcheck that install.ps1:20 now installs (tied to known correctness-MAJ-16-r1). context/actions/implementing.md and context/rules/plan.md differ in the worktree from the commit (review-context overlay); no findings there.

findings.claim: The new hash_explained_anywhere helper (lines 111-118) is placed between squash_contained and filter_untracked, 150 lines above the explained_pairs global it iterates (declared line 268) and its siblings mark_explained/is_explained (269-278); a top-to-bottom reader meets a loop over explained_pairs before the array and its contract comment exist, and the near-identical loop body of is_explained sits elsewhere.
findings.evidence: Re-read verdict.sh in full at 1f725ce: hash_explained_anywhere at 111-118 loops `${explained_pairs[@]+...}`; explained_pairs=() and its 'hash<->candidate explanations' contract comment are at 263-268, is_explained at 272-278 with the same loop shape. Every other helper in the lib is declared next to the global it owns (cherry_plus/compute_cherry_sets, verdict/probe_verdict, verdict_hashes/verdict_for).
findings.fix: Move hash_explained_anywhere directly below is_explained (after line 278), next to the explained_pairs declaration it reads.

findings.claim: The new `|| squash_contained "$from" "$branch"` clause runs a git merge-tree for every branch with all_transferred=0, including the common case of a local FROM (main), where the guarded body only scans candidates, sets is_candidate=1 and does nothing; for a local FROM the same merge-tree was already computed by the layer-4 loop at 453-463, so the clause is dead work whose position suggests it matters for local FROMs.
findings.evidence: Re-read evaluate_branch 417-519: is_candidate starts 0 (420) and is only set in the early-return path (431-433) or inside this block (512-514); the block's only effect is the eval_in prepend guarded by is_candidate -eq 0 (515-517), i.e. remote-tracking FROM only. The comment at 508-510 itself states a local FROM 'already earned its star via candidate_fully_explained'.
findings.fix: Resolve is_candidate first (or use candidate_index "$from" -lt 0) and evaluate squash_contained only for a non-candidate FROM: `if [ "$(candidate_index "$from")" -lt 0 ] && { [ "$all_transferred" -eq 1 ] || squash_contained "$from" "$branch"; }; then eval_in="$from*..."; fi`.

findings.claim: peekIdentity issues its /healthz probe with client.Get and takes no context, although its only caller startPeek holds the server's signal ctx; the context chain is broken at the new helper, so a SIGTERM/Ctrl-C arriving during startup does not cancel the probe, while the sibling installer probe (install_windows.go verifyServing) builds its request with http.NewRequestWithContext.
findings.evidence: Re-read main.go 223-238 and 245-247: `func peekIdentity(addr string)`, `client.Get("http://" + addr + "/healthz")`; startPeek(ctx, ...) calls peekIdentity(addr) without ctx. install_windows.go 262 uses http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, url, nil) — the in-repo pattern.
findings.fix: Change to `func peekIdentity(ctx context.Context, addr string)`, build the request with http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, url, nil) and client.Do, and pass ctx from startPeek.

findings.claim: The control-port branch appends to args twice in a row (`args = append(args, "--control-port", ...)` then `args = append(args, "--back-link", backLink)`) where one variadic append carries both flag pairs.
findings.evidence: Re-read main.go 260-265: two consecutive append statements on the same slice inside the same `if controlPort != 0` block, no logic between them.
findings.fix: Merge into one call: `args = append(args, "--control-port", strconv.Itoa(controlPort), "--back-link", backLink)` (multiline per RULE-GOLANG-CALL-001).
